I read the code at bc7090d. In src/cli.ts:769 the listing warnings are printed as `warning: ${'--plugin-dir'|'--openai-manifest'} ${scrub(e.path, redactor)} ${scrub(e.message, redactor)}`. scrub only redacts secrets. This line never goes through visibleText or ciSafeLine. Elsewhere those helpers are used on the --verbose dump (line 817), the [http] and stdio tail lines (821-822), the fatal path (897) and the config notices (570/573), but not here, and nothing sanitizes stderr later before it is returned (lines 823 and 876-878 only scrub or append).

The path comes from file content. In src/listing/load.ts:236-250, declaredMcp() takes the manifest's string `mcpServers`, strips `./` and builds `shown` with posix(), which only swaps backslashes for slashes (displayUrl is used only when the value has a scheme). Then it calls `listing.errors.push({source:'openai', path: shown, ...})`. The plugin-dir errors use relative file names (rel) the same way.

I reproduced it in a detached worktree at bc7090d after npm ci and a build. I copied test/fixtures/listing/openai-valid to the scratchpad and set mcpServers to "./x\u001b[31mRED\n::error title=Injected::forged annotation\n##[error]legacy", then ran `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true node dist/cli.js --format json --openai-manifest .../plugin.json`. It exited 0. `cat -v` of stderr showed `warning: --openai-manifest x^[[31mRED`, then a line of its own reading `::error title=Injected::forged annotation`, then a line starting with `##[error]legacy does not exist in the package ...`. So the ESC byte reaches the terminal raw, and a workflow command starts a new line. The LST-024 annotation for the same problem, printed right after, is escaped correctly (`\u{1B}`, `%0A`, `#\u{23}[`), which matches the claim.

This is the same class as the round-3 fixes A07-04/A07-07, so medium fits: it needs a manifest supplied by a PR in CI and lets that PR forge annotations, stop-commands or add-mask. The fix is to wrap the line in ciSafeLine/visibleText. I removed the worktree afterwards.
